headline: Approved a motion backing timely action on visitor parking plaques and authorized engaging Ansa Stamper for rebranding.
summary: The meeting covered the Director's report on social services, transportation, dining, and programs, plus new business on parking, rebranding, and the Friends' report. Members approved the June 17, 2026 minutes, supported timely action on visitor parking, and authorized rebranding work with Ansa Stamper. The city placed organizing snow shoveling on hold.
decisions: Approved the June 17, 2026 regular meeting minutes by unanimous roll call vote.
Approved a motion that the COA support timely action on the visitor parking issue and reinstating physical visitor parking plaques as an option, by unanimous roll call vote.
Authorized the director to engage Ansa Stamper for a rebranding process; the motion passed unanimously.
Updated the approved amount for CVS and Market Basket gift cards for the Social Services team to $2,500.
The city placed organizing snow shoveling on hold.

1 
 
 
SALEM COUNCIL ON AGING & SENIOR SERVICES 
REGULAR MONTHLY MEETING MINUTES 
 
Date and Time:  September 16, 2026 at 5:15 p.m.  
Meeting Location:  Levesque Community Life Center Conference Room 
401 Bridge Street, Salem, MA 
 
Members Present:  Lynda Coffill (LC, Chair), John Russell (JR, Vice Chair), Abigail 
Butt (AB, Treasurer), Kristin Macek (KM, Secretary); George 
Barbuzzi (GB), Michelle Bettencourt (MB), and Patricia Small 
(PS)     
Absent: Eliud Alcala (EA) and James Eric Rogers (JER) 
Also Present:  Teresa Arnold, (TA, Director of the COA & Senior Services); 
Councilor Lydia King and Clerk Joanne M. Roomey 
 
I. MEETING CALLED TO ORDER  
LC called the meeting to order at 5:15 p.m.  
II. APPROVAL OF THE JUNE 17, 2026 REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  
A motion was made by JR  to approve the June 17, 2026, Regular Meeting Minutes . 
Seconded by PS. A roll call vote was taken, and the motion was carried unanimously.    
III. DIRECTOR’S REPORT 
Social Services: 
• We welcomed back one of our SHINE volunteers who has been out for over a year. 
This brings us to three volunteers each taking three appointments per week, which is 
very helpful to the Social Services team. The two licensed social workers are also 
SHINE-certified. 
• Ingrid Patterson has been conducting outreach every Wednesday with Julio Mota from 
the Mayor’s office in various neighborhoods informing them of COA/ CLC services. 
She is also attending various events in the community to spread the word. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
DOMINICK PANGALLO                 
MAYOR 
 
 
CITY OF SALEM, MASSACHUSETTS 
COUNCIL ON AGING & 
SENIOR SERVICES BOARD 
401 BRIDGE STREET  
SALEM, MA  01970 
TEL: 9787440924 
 
 
 
 
 
 
LYNDA COFFILL, CHAIR 
JOHN RUSSELL, VICE CHAIR 
 
    TERESA GOVE ARNOLD 
 DIRECTOR
2 
 
• The Social Services team is gearing up to assist with Medicare Open Enrollment, Fuel 
assistance, and Property Tax Exemption applications. 
• 100 seniors received $25 in Farmers Market Coupons. This is a great program through 
the Department of Agriculture which promotes healthy eating and supports our local 
farmers. Everyone was very appreciative of these coupons. 
• The COA h osted the Assessors Tax Relief Workshop on September 10. Assessor 
Stephen Cortes presented . Five people went to T A after the presentation to make 
appointments to see if they are eligible for the Tax Work Off program.  
Activities/Programs: 
• Today, the Council on Aging co- hosted a Resource Fair with the Disability Resource 
Center. Forty-five health, wellness, and service organizations participated. 
• The Salem Rotary Club will host a Back -to-the-70s event from 4:00- 7:00 pm on 
September 24. 
• Chromebook classes with Kevin Figueroa are under way, and 18 people will receive a 
free Chromebook upon successful completion of the class. The computers were 
purchased with the last of funds from a Tech Equity Grant from the State. 
• Anne Boris is teaching Spanish classes with rave reviews. The first six-week session is 
nearly complete, and we already have a full class for the next session. 
• We have a large entry in the Haunted Happenings Parade with Alice in Wonderland as 
our theme. Staff and Board members will dress up as main characters, and we have a 
dance troupe, a decorated van and two trolleys for seniors to ride. 
Transportation: 
• We have been down two drivers for the last few weeks; one due to a death in the family 
and one had surgery. Other  drivers have bee n helpful  working additional hours as 
needed. 
• Electric vehicles are not helpful to our population. Those with mobility issues find them 
hard to navigate, so they are not used as frequently as we had hoped. There are 
challenges with charging in extreme heat and extreme cold. This has been an issue with 
other Councils on Aging and organizations who use EVs. TA has informed Neal Duffy, 
Sustainability Director of the city. TA wonders if another department might benefit 
from using the EVs but needs to check the grant terms with Mass DOT. 
Dining Services/Kitchen Update: 
• Erica Blumberg retired on August 21. We have hired Suzanne Harrigan as a part -time 
temporary employee to manage the morning café and lunch operations. She started on 
September 9.
3 
 
• Per Mike Crounse, Facilities Director for the city: “Rough electrical is complete and 
has been inspected  by the electrical inspector. Rough plumbing is underway. The 
plumber has not yet been able to schedule his rough inspection. We cut and excavated 
the slab and exposed the 4" drain line. The plumber has made his connection to it. 
Siding has been received a nd installed at the former window openings. The HVAC 
contractor will be on site tomorrow to begin setting up supports and, if we make good 
progress, start hanging the hood. He is scheduled to be there the rest of the week.” Mr. 
Crounse will continue to update CLC leadership. 
• Request for Proposals to manage the kitchen operations will close on September 18. 
Memory Café/Reiki Clinic: 
• The monthly Reiki Clinic held on September 10 was full and there was a wait list. 
• The monthly Memory Café will host Karen Coppola, a dementia practitioner with the 
"It Takes a Herd" program. She will be visiting with therapeutic mini horses from Lazy 
J Ranch on September 24 at 1:00 pm. 
Other: 
• The nursing students from Salem State started back today, and Dr. Poremba will lead 
two cohorts; one on Wednesdays and one on Thursdays for six- week rotations during 
the academic year. North Shore Community College nursing students will visit on 
Thursdays and Fridays from October to December. Both Salem State and NSCC 
students are here to study the social determinants of health. 
• The COA and the Veteran’s Department will cohost an event on November 10 to 
present the story of Salemite Nelson “Sparky” Nersasian who was one of the 28 men 
to survive the torpedoing and sinking of destroyer USS Leopold in 1944. Bob 
Nersasian, who wrote the book Never to Return, will be with us. 
• Looking ahead, we will hold our annual Remembrance Ceremony on November 17. 
IV. OLD BUSINESS:  
a. Senior Housing:  
Beacon Communities will host an open house for Lee Fort Terrace on Monday, 
September 28. Please let TA know if you want to attend. 
b. Snow Shoveling 
The Mayor’s Office discussed the proposal and noted that liability is a significant 
concern, as well as the difficulty of recruiting students, even when compensation is 
offered. The city  has decided to place organizing snow shoveling on hold. TA 
suggested that neighborhood associations would better know who needs snow 
shoveling assistance in their respective areas.
4 
 
Councilor King noted that the mayor suggested ward councilors help connect residents 
with one another, rather than manage the program. There was a suggestion for inviting 
students to a meeting and promoting the opportunity through the schools, allowing 
them to volunteer as neighborhood helpers while minimizing liability concerns. PS 
noted that she had read about communities where students receive school credit for 
volunteering. MB suggested holding a neighborhood job fair. 
It was noted that the city  is responsible for maintaining the schools, streets, and 
sidewalks, but currently has only one employee and one machine available for this 
work. 
c. Senior Day Recap 
GB said there was a great turnout. A thank-you note should be sent to John Harvey for 
supplying the tent, ice cream, macaroni and cheese, and baked beans. 
d. CLC KITCHEN 
TA addressed this in the Director's Report. 
V. NEW BUSINESS:   
a. Resident and Visitor Parking Passes 
GB raised concerns regarding residents and visitor parking passes. AB noted that 
parking is very limited in the neighborhood, particularly for residents without 
driveways, and suggested that the city consider restricting parking to one side of the 
street.  
LC mentioned that a new family in her  neighborhood has six vehicles, further 
contributing to the parking shortage. Councilor King stated that she and Conrad 
Prosniewski have been working to reinstate a physical plaque system for visitor 
parking, as obtaining parking passes can be difficult for residents. A meeting had been 
scheduled to discuss the issue but was cancelled. Councilor King noted that parking 
regulations differ between downtown and residential areas and that another committee 
meeting is being sought. 
The Councilor stated that the m ayor and Transportation Department are the primary 
contacts regarding the issue. The COA has not taken a formal position, but LC 
questioned whether the issue could be resolved by reinstating physical visitor parking 
plaques as an option. It was noted that the issue particularly affects homecare providers 
and others who need to visit older residents. 
Councilor King suggested writing  a letter to the mayor  regarding the issue . AB 
suggested involving Lisa Cammarata from HR.
5 
 
JR made a motion that the COA support timely action to address the visitor parking 
issue and reinstating physical visitor parking plaques as an option. AB seconded the 
motion. A roll call vote was taken, and the motion was carried unanimously. Chair LC 
will write an email to the mayor.  
b. Rebranding 
AB worked with Ansa Stamper for Lincoln COA rebranding and referred TA to her. 
TA did make initial contact, and Ms. Stamper was to be in touch with TA after Labor 
Day. TA emailed again and is waiting for a reply. AB will reach out as well.  
AB made a motion to authorize TA to engage Ansa Stamper for a rebranding process. 
MB seconded the motion. The motion passed unanimously.  
AB also mentioned that Microsoft Publisher is no longer available, and that Councils 
on Aging must transition to Canva for the newsletter. The transition has presented some 
challenges for various users. 
c. Women’s Expo 2027 
MB reported that the planning meeting held the previous day went well. The committee 
identified approximately 15 potential businesses to approach regarding sponsorship of 
activities. MB also presented a draft flyer, which will be revised and distributed to 
vendors for advertising closer to the event in February. 
d. Lee Fort Terrace Ribbon Cutting September 28 at 9:00 a.m. 
LC noted that anyone who is available is welcome to attend the ribbon- cutting 
ceremony. PS, JR, and staff member Ingrid Patterson have already toured the facility. 
e. Friends of the COA Report  
JR reported that the Friends held their first meeting in a while and welcomed two new 
members, attorney Laurie Weisman, and John Harvey.  
The group discussed upcoming Halloween activities, with parking in the CLC lot 
scheduled to begin the weekend of September 15, as well as food trucks scheduled for 
the same weekend. The Friends have a QR code, which needs to be updated. 
JR reported that the annual appeal letters sent in mid-June raised approximately 
$20,000. AB said some recipients received letters that did not include a date or 
indicate the amount of their previous contribution. JR stated that he would address the 
issue with Friends Chairperson Bonnie Belair and that the Friends will follow up with 
thank-you letters to donors.  
The amount approved for CVS and Market Basket gift cards for the Social Services 
team to distribute as needed was updated to $2,500.
6 
 
JR also reported that the Friends experienced an issue with their accountant regarding 
the filing of taxes. They have since retained a new accountant. 
VI. OTHER BUSINESS: None 
VII. ANNUAL MEETING AND NEXT BOARD MEETING: Wednesday, October 21, 
2026 at 5:15 p.m. and 5:30 p.m. ON ZOOM ONLY 
 
VIII. VOTE TO ADJOURN 
There being no further business to come before the C OA & Senior Services  Board this 
evening; JR moved to adjourn the meeting. Seconded by AB . A roll call vote was taken,  
and the motion was carried unanimously. The meeting adjourned at 6:20 p.m.  
Respectfully Submitted, 
  
 
Joanne M. Roomey 
Board Clerk 
 
Know Your Rights under the Open Meeting Law M.G.L. Chapter 30A ss. 1825 and City Ordinance  
Sections 22028 through 22033.
